purpose: Deterministic known-bad patterns in a book's Georgian copy. A hit FLAGS the book for human review and is recorded on the run. Nothing here ever rewrites a word: this file is a reading aid for a person, not an editor. Correcting the text is the story-polish pass's job (StoryPolishPrompt), and a rule that silently repaired a book would hide the fact that the polish missed it.
scope: Story text and the title of a composite-pipeline book, after the polish pass. Never the English fields, never the scene descriptions, never a model prompt.

rules.note: Shipped in a completed book as ფუნღუროში. The stem is ფუღურ- (hollow, tree hollow); the inserted ნ is a misspelling, not a dialect form. Matched as a stem so every case ending is caught.

rules.expected: Georgian case suffixes attach directly to the name: თემოს, not თემო-ს.
rules.note: Shipped in a completed book as თემო-ს. The hyphen comes from personalization templating that concatenates the child's name with a suffix; a Georgian noun takes its ending with no separator. Flagged rather than repaired because the fix belongs where the concatenation happens (R12a), and a book already carrying it needs a person to look at every occurrence.

rules.expected: იყოს, or ეგდოს where the sense is 'to lie / be lying there'
rules.note: Shipped in a completed book. ეწყოს is a real word, so this is a verb-choice flag rather than a spelling one: in the sentence it appeared in, the sense wanted იყოს (to be) or ეგდოს (to lie there). A human decides which; this rule only makes sure nobody has to notice it in a printed proof.

rules.expected: მას ეძინება — the everyday spoken form, pending Georgian editor approval
rules.note: v1.1, from the supplier's audit-2 finding P1-07: the shipped book said მას ძილი ნებავს to a two-year-old. ნებავს is a real word and a bookish one, so this is a register flag rather than a spelling one — the audit's own suggested replacement is მას ეძინება 'if approved by the Georgian editor', which is exactly why this flags and never rewrites. The composite story prompt (composite-v1.1) asks for the natural form; this rule catches the book where the ask did not land.

rules.expected: One simple tense for the whole book — the present, unless the book is written in the past throughout
rules.note: v1.1, from audit-2 finding P1-07: the shipped book alternated ქრება/ანათებს with გამოვიდა/გაჰყვნენ/აინთო. The rule fires when one page carries both a present-tense form (a word ending -ება/-ებს/-ავს/-ობს) and a preverbed aorist (გამოვიდა, გაჰყვნენ, აინთო), which is the strongest signal a deterministic reading can take: this check sees one location at a time, so a book that is present on spread 3 and past on spread 5 is invisible to it and stays the Georgian editor's read. Dialogue may legitimately speak in another tense while the narration holds one — a person decides, which is the whole contract of this file.

The companion's name is ბეკი in every grammatical form, always with კ. BekiIdentityRules.EnforceBrandSpelling already corrects this deterministically on the legacy path; the rule is here so that a book which somehow reaches storage with ქ is flagged rather than printed.
